relationships.claim: The atrioventricular node produces the slow-conduction, long-refractory-period delay between atrial and ventricular activation that coordinates sequential chamber contraction, and it filters rapid atrial impulses that could otherwise conduct to the ventricles.

Coronary blood flow supplies the working myocardium with oxygen and metabolic substrate, and because resting oxygen extraction is already high, increased myocardial oxygen demand is met mainly by increasing coronary flow rather than by extracting further oxygen.

Within a physiologic range, greater ventricular end-diastolic stretch of myocardial fibers increases the force of the subsequent contraction, so stroke volume rises as preload rises, up to the point where further stretch no longer increases contractile force.
